title: Dedicated throughput boundary spec and SLA notice procedures
creator: Jordan Patel
description:
Background:
This ticket centralizes a distinct 'throughput boundary' spec for Dedicated customers and a prescriptive notification + remediation procedure that legal, SRE, and account teams can rely on. Existing artifacts proliferate variations of credit formulas and error-budget logic; we need a single canonical spec that ties the measurement windows, burst handling, autoscaler interlock, and customer notice templates together.

Goals:
- Define measurable SLA metric(s) for Dedicated throughput that are simple for contract language and implementable in telemetry.
- Specify error budget computation using fixed windows and warm-start adjustments (to avoid false positives during rolling upgrades).
- Document autoscaler interlocks and fleet control rules that should pause crediting/trigger emergency capacity.
- Provide templated customer notices and an operational playbook for remediation, credit calculation, and dispute handling.

Scope / Non-goals:
- Includes: throughput floor definition, measurement queries, degradation classification, credit formula, notification cadence, sample contract language, interaction with autoscaler.
- Excludes: legal negotiation language beyond templates; pricing changes.

Proposed definitions (key terms):
- Throughput Window: 10-minute moving window measured per-tenant across reserved pool(s).
- Guaranteed Throughput (GT): tokens/s committed in contract (converted to per-minute and per-10-minute buckets).
- Capacity Corridor: a safely-serve band (GT minus 10% to GT + 20%) where autoscaler and graceful-degrade rules have different behaviors.
- Error Budget: cumulative minutes in a 30-day rolling period where effective serve rate falls below GT. Credits are issued only when Error Budget burn exceeds threshold T.

Measurement algorithm (summary):
1) Compute per-minute effective serve rate = successful_output_tokens / served_wall_time for each minute.
2) Smooth with 3-sample median filter to ignore single-minute spikes from autoscaler churn.
3) Mark a minute as 'degraded' if effective serve rate < 0.9 * GT (per-contract conversion).
4) Error Budget (30-day) = sum(degraded_minutes) / 30-day total minutes.
5) Credit trigger: if Error Budget > 2% sustained over any 72-hour window, begin remediation workflow.

Credit computation (example):
- Proportional credit = min( (degraded_minutes / total_guaranteed_minutes) * committed_monthly_fee, committed_monthly_fee ) rounded to nearest dollar.
- Burst exemptions: short bursts (<= 5 consecutive degraded minutes per incident, and total < 0.1% monthly) are exempted from credits to avoid noisy short blips.

Autoscaler and fleet interlock rules:
- Autoscaler warm-up detection: after scaling events we mark a 15-minute warm-start window where minutes are not counted toward credit if hardware provisioning signals are present.
- Global throttling vs tenant-specific throttling: when global mitigations run (e.g., AZ level capacity pressure), credits accrue per-tenant but remediation route prioritizes multi-tenant failover obligations first before tenant credits.
- Forced failover policy: if an AZ goes unhealthy and traffic moves to a secondary AZ, we do not count the first 30 minutes post-failover toward credits if documented failover runbook executed.

Operational playbook (high level):
- Detection: Alerting rules on 72h rolling Error Budget > 2% and a separate P0 alert for sustained 95th-percentile latency degradation aligned to throughput drops.
- Incident run: SRE oncall opens dedicated investigation channel, triages whether degradation caused by infra, autoscaler policy, model kernel regressions, or customer-induced traffic patterns.
- Customer notice: Tiered templates: (a) Initial notice within 30 minutes of remediation workflow start; (b) Follow-up within 4 hours with root cause hypothesis; (c) Resolution + credits summary within 10 business days. Sample notice links: https://confluence.internal.redwood/dedicated/sla-notices (placeholder).
- Credit issuance: Finance issues credit after post-mortem confirms measurement window and burn calculation. Credits appear on next billing cycle with reference code.

Customer dispute path:
1) Customer submits evidence within 30 days of invoice.
2) Dedicated PM and SRE validate telemetry queries (include saved Grafana queries) and rerun computations in a reproducible notebook.
3) If disagreement persists, escalate to legal for binding arbitration per contract clause.

Artifacts / links referenced:
- Dashboard: grafana/redwood/dedicated/throughput-boundary (saved queries required)
- Telemetry queries (KQL): saved query ids: dq_throughput_window_v2, dq_degraded_minute_v1
- Example GitHub PR for telemetry pipeline changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/1234 (PR: add median smoothing and warm-start flags)
- Draft customer notice templates: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1DUMMYLINK

Open decisions / trade-offs noted during sync with Legal & SRE:
- Measurement window length: 10-minute windows reduce noise but lengthen time-to-detect; proposal is conservative to protect customers.
- Warm-start exemptions: SRE pushed for 30-minute warm-start, Legal prefers 15 minutes. Compromise: 15 minutes for autoscaler rapid events, 30 minutes for large cluster reprovision.
- Burstable credits: whether to allow single-month cumulative burst forgiveness. Proposed: allow burst exemptions up to 0.1% monthly to reduce noisy credits.

Next steps & action items:
- PM: finalize contract template language and circulate to Sales/Legal by 2026-02-20.
- SRE: produce reproducible telemetry notebook and add saved queries by 2026-02-05 (owner: @sre-lead).
- Engineering: implement median filter and warm-start flag in telemetry pipeline; land PR and coordinate deploy by 2026-02-14. Link to PR above.
- Design/Console: add dedicated SLA panel to Console showing GT, current Error Budget, projected credit exposure; mock due 2026-01-25.

Acceptance criteria:
- Signed-off contract template with 1-page SLA clause and credit appendix.
- Telemetry queries and notebook reproduce credit calculations deterministically.
- Console panel mock approved by Design and Product.
- Sample customer notices approved by Legal.

Risks / mitigation:
- Risk: Measurement complexity leads to disputes. Mitigation: publish exact SQL/KQL and reproducible notebook used for billing.
- Risk: Autoscaler churn generating false positives. Mitigation: warm-start windows and median smoothing plus burst exemptions.
